about: EventBridge's schedule expressions as its documentation gives them, and their next runs: the table the backend's reader (schedule-expression.ts) and ff's read for their tests, so that both read an expression alike. Times are UTC. A test's cases run each expression's next runs after `after`: as many as `runs` lists, or `count` when fewer remain; from `anchor`, a rate's first run, when one is given.

refused.title: rate(1 minutes)
refused.message: rate(1 minutes) must be rate(1 minute): the unit is singular for 1

refused.title: rate(5 minute)
refused.message: rate(5 minute) must be rate(5 minutes): the unit is plural above 1

refused.title: rate(0 minutes)
refused.message: rate() takes a value of 1 or more

refused.title: rate(5 seconds)
refused.message: rate() takes minute(s), hour(s) or day(s), not "seconds"

refused.title: rate(1.5 hours)
refused.message: rate() takes a whole number and a unit, such as rate(5 minutes)

refused.title: rate(-1 day)
refused.message: rate() takes a whole number and a unit, such as rate(5 minutes)

refused.title: rate(5 constructors)
refused.message: rate() takes minute(s), hour(s) or day(s), not "constructors"

refused.title: five fields
refused.message: cron() takes six fields, minutes hours day-of-month month day-of-week year; got 5

refused.title: both days
refused.message: cron(): one of the day-of-month and day-of-week fields must be "?", and only one: the other says which days

refused.title: neither day
refused.message: cron(): one of the day-of-month and day-of-week fields must be "?", and only one: the other says which days

refused.title: "?" for the hours
refused.message: cron(): the hours field can't be "?": only the day-of-month or the day-of-week can

refused.title: minute 60
refused.message: cron(): the minutes field takes 0 to 59; got 60

refused.title: hour 24
refused.message: cron(): the hours field takes 0 to 23; got 24

refused.title: day 32
refused.message: cron(): the day-of-month field takes 1 to 31; got 32

refused.title: month 13
refused.message: cron(): the month field takes 1 to 12; got 13

refused.title: a day of the week 8
refused.message: cron(): the day-of-week field takes 1 to 7; got 8

refused.title: a year before 1970
refused.message: cron(): the year field takes 1970 to 2199; got 1969

refused.title: a name that is none
refused.message: cron(): "FUN" is not a value of the day-of-week field

refused.title: a sixth week
refused.message: cron(): "2#6" must be a day and its week in the month, 1 to 5, such as 2#1, the first Monday

refused.title: W where it means nothing
refused.message: cron(): "W" is not an item of the day-of-month field: L, LW and nW are

refused.title: a step of 0
refused.message: cron(): the step in "0/0" must be a whole number of 1 or more

refused.title: seconds, more often than once a minute
refused.message: cron() takes six fields, minutes hours day-of-month month day-of-week year; got 7

refused.title: neither rate nor cron
refused.message: A schedule is rate(value unit), such as rate(5 minutes), or cron(minutes hours day-of-month month day-of-week year), such as cron(0 8 * * ? *)

runs.title: rate(): runs every interval from its first run, which a late run doesn't move

cases.note: Late by 12 minutes: the next is the first of its runs after now, not one per run missed.

runs.title: rate(): has no run after 2199, where cron's years end, however long its interval

cases.note: Beyond what a Date holds, these would make an invalid date: none instead.

runs.title: cron(): runs cron(0 10 * * ? *) as EventBridge's documentation says
cron(): runs cron(15 12 * * ? *) as EventBridge's documentation says
cron(): runs cron(0 18 ? * MON-FRI *) as EventBridge's documentation says
cron(): runs cron(0 8 1 * ? *) as EventBridge's documentation says
cron(): runs cron(0/15 * * * ? *) as EventBridge's documentation says
cron(): runs cron(0/10 * ? * MON-FRI *) as EventBridge's documentation says

cases.note: Saturday the 24th: the next is Monday's first.

runs.title: cron(): runs cron(0/5 8-17 ? * MON-FRI *) as EventBridge's documentation says
cron(): runs cron(0 9 ? * 2#1 *) as EventBridge's documentation says

cases.note: The first Monday of each month.

runs.title: cron(): runs strictly after the time, to the minute, in UTC
cron(): takes the last day of the month, L, in February of a leap year and not
cron(): takes the last weekday of the month, LW, and the weekday nearest a day, W, without leaving the month

cases.note: 2026-10-31 is a Saturday: the last weekday is Friday the 30th; 2027-01-31 a Sunday: Friday the 29th.
2026-08-01 is a Saturday: 1W is Monday the 3rd, never July's 31st.
2026-05-31 is a Sunday, the month's last day: 31W is Friday the 29th; months without a 31st have none.

runs.title: cron(): takes a day of the week's last in the month, nL, and the nth, # — skipping the months without a fifth

cases.note: The last Friday (6) of each month.
The fifth Thursday (5): October 2026 has one (the 29th), November none (its Thursdays end on the 26th), December the 31st.

runs.title: cron(): takes names for months and days, in any case, and "L" alone for Saturday
cron(): wraps a range around its end: 20-2 is 20:00 to 02:00, FRI-MON the weekend
cron(): takes steps from a value, from a range, and from *, and lists
cron(): runs within its years, and no more after them
